# Notes HTTP API (brownfield feature)

Add an HTTP API in front of the existing notes library.

## Requirements
- `POST /notes` with JSON {title, body} creates a note (201 + the note incl. id); an empty title returns 400.
- `GET /notes` lists notes; `GET /notes/:id` returns one note or 404.
- `GET /search?q=term` returns matching notes using the existing search function; an empty `q` returns 400.
- `GET /health` returns 200 {"status":"ok"}.
- Reuse the existing NoteStore and searchNotes. Follow the repository's existing conventions (see its README and tooling): library functions never throw and return Result<T>; HTTP status mapping happens only at the edge. No new runtime dependencies (use node:http).
- Deployment: `Dockerfile` (node:24-alpine) and `docker-compose.yml` exposing the service on host port 8081; `scripts/smoke.ts` run by `npm run smoke` exercises /health, creating a note, fetching it and searching it against http://localhost:8081, exiting non-zero on any failure.

## Non-functional requirements
- Every endpoint responds in under 50 ms (p95) locally for up to 1,000 stored notes.
- The 5 existing tests keep passing and the lint complexity limit (8) and type check stay clean.
- The service logs one line per request and never logs request bodies.

- **AC-3** `POST /notes` with a body that is not valid JSON, or whose `title`/`body` are not strings, returns 400 with an `error` message and stores no note.

- **AC-11** Each request writes exactly one log line to stdout of the form `<METHOD> <path> <status> <duration>ms`; the line never contains the request body or query string (a test posting a body containing a unique marker finds 0 log lines containing that marker).

- **AC-14** A `Dockerfile` based on `node:24-alpine` exists at the repo root and `docker build .` exits 0.
- **AC-15** `docker-compose.yml` at the repo root publishes the service on host port 8081; after `docker compose up -d`, `curl -fsS http://localhost:8081/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}` within 120 s.

## Why
`notes-lib` is an in-memory notes library (`NoteStore`, `searchNotes`, `Result<T>`) that is only
usable in-process. We want other programs to create, read and search notes over HTTP, and to run
the service as a container, without rewriting the library and without breaking its conventions:
library functions never throw and return `Result<T>`, files are kebab-case, tests live in `tests/`
and run with `npm test` (node:test), lint is ESLint (complexity 8, 40 lines per function) and the
type check is `tsc --noEmit`.

The HTTP layer is a thin edge: it parses requests, calls the existing `NoteStore` / `searchNotes`,
and is the only place where a `Result` error is mapped to an HTTP status code. No runtime
dependencies are added; the server uses `node:http`.

## Success criteria
- 5 endpoints are served: `POST /notes`, `GET /notes`, `GET /notes/:id`, `GET /search?q=`, `GET /health`.
- Status codes match the PRD exactly: 201 on create, 200 on reads and health, 400 for an empty title or empty `q`, 404 for an unknown note id.
- p95 latency of every endpoint is under 50 ms locally with 1,000 stored notes (measured by an automated test over at least 100 requests per endpoint).
- All 5 existing tests still pass unchanged; `npm run lint` (complexity limit 8) and `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
- 0 new entries in `dependencies` in `package.json`.
- Exactly 1 log line per request, and 0 log lines contain request body content.
- `docker compose up -d` serves `GET http://localhost:8081/health` with 200 within 120 s.
- `npm run smoke` exits 0 against a running service and exits with a non-zero code on any failed step.

## Non-goals
- Persistence: notes stay in memory and are lost on restart (same as the library today).
- Update/delete endpoints, authentication, pagination, CORS.
- Changing the public library API in `src/index.ts`, `src/note-store.ts`, `src/search.ts` or `src/result.ts`.
